meta_description: Foundation models are converging on capability; the durable advantage sits in retrieval, permissions and freshness.

blocks.x: Foundation models are converging on capability; the durable advantage sits in retrieval, permissions and freshness.

The argument for The retrieval layer is the moat, not the model is simple: decisions made on stale information cost more than the platform that would make them current — and the gap is measurable in weeks, not years.

items: Every enterprise answer should cite its source paragraph — provenance is the feature that survives audit.
Permission-aware retrieval turns your existing entitlements into AI guardrails for free.
Freshness SLAs on corpora are the difference between trusted assistants and abandoned demos.

blocks.x: Three questions to ask your current vendors

items: Ask for the baseline: how was the starting position measured, and who signed it?
Ask for the trail: can your auditors replay any decision the system made last week, end to end?
Ask for the unit cost: what does one decision cost to run, and who owns keeping it down?

blocks.x: Programs like The retrieval layer is the moat, not the model rarely fail on the technology. They fail on unnamed ownership, unmeasured baselines and ungated scope — the three failure modes the guards on this page are built for.

items: Every stage has a gate with real stop authority — scope expands on measured deltas, not on momentum.
The operating model is designed first — who decides what, at which gate, holding which evidence.
Evidence is generated while the work happens, so the audit is a walkthrough, not an archaeology project.

blocks.x: Grounded-answer rates above 92% are achievable when retrieval is engineered, not appended.
